references.text: Isaiah opens his prophecy with the same appeal to heaven and earth as witnesses, just as Moses does in his farewell song.
Jeremiah also calls upon heaven to be a witness against Israel's sin, using similar poetic language.
The psalm calls upon heaven and earth as witnesses when God judges His people, the same cosmic appeal for testimony.
Micah calls upon the mountains and the foundations of the earth to hear the Lord's case against Israel, a similar legal summons for witnesses.
Earlier in Deuteronomy, Moses takes heaven and earth as witnesses against Israel, using the same legal formula for testimony.
Moses again takes heaven and earth as witnesses when he presents the choice between life and death to the people.
Moses calls upon heaven and earth as witnesses just before he delivers the song, providing direct context for verse 32:1.
The heavens declare God's glory, a similar theme of heaven conveying God's word and testimony.
